chapter: Imperial Orchestra and Southern Rhythm Boys
title: Hart asks for Nellie to join the Imperial Orchestra
summary: When pianist Al Freeman went home to Ohio, Clarence Hart proposed Nellie; her father agreed but her mother hesitated.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So they would wake me up and I would start playing, you know, and it was -- that was an awful lot of fun, and that's something that helped me an awful, awful lot. And then of course later on I -- they needed a pianist in the orchestra, because there was a piano player from Columbus, Ohio by the name of Al Freeman, and Al Freeman was a marvelous pianist, just marvelous, and he'd lived in Lake Charles for quite some time, and he decided to go back to his home town in Columbus, and he left, and of course they didn't have a piano player. They needed someone. So they were trying to locate, trying to find a piano player, and so Mr. Harts, who was the leader of the Imperial Orchestra and he said to my father, he said, 'Well, what about Nellie?' He said, 'Nellie plays well enough to play with us.' So my dad says, he says -- my dad was all for

it and he said, "Well, I think she can play well enough to play with us," you know, because sometimes at the house my dad and I would play, you know. He would be playing and I would play along with him. But my mother wasn't too keen on it. She didn't think too much of the idea. Well, of course it was a natural thing at that time, this was a biased thing, in thinking about religion and music, you know. And many people felt -- this was the general, not many, but it was the general feeling, somehow they looked down at jazz music, you know, and as I get older, and as I got older, I realized how stupid it was because you were only expressing a natural gift and a natural talent.
